desc:
A cashier has an unlimited supply of coins of each value listed in coins. An amount is payable if it can be written as a sum of coins (a coin may be used many times).

Return how many integers in the range 1..limit are not payable.

coins = [3,5], limit = 10 -> 4   (1, 2, 4 and 7 cannot be paid)
coins = [4,6], limit = 12 -> 7   (only 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 can be paid)
coins = [1],   limit = 5  -> 0
hints: Instead of counting the bad amounts directly, decide for each amount from 1 up whether it is payable.
An amount s is payable exactly when s - c is payable for some coin c ≤ s, with 0 counted as payable.
Keep a boolean array reachable[0..limit] with reachable[0] = true, fill it from left to right, and count the false entries among 1..limit.
editorial: Let reachable[s] say whether amount s can be paid. The empty payment gives reachable[0] = true. For s ≥ 1, think of the last coin c of some payment: removing it leaves a payment of s - c. So s is payable exactly when reachable[s - c] holds for at least one coin c ≤ s.

Fill the array from small to large amounts and count the entries in 1..limit that stay false. This is the boolean version of coin change, with O(limit · n) time and O(limit) space. (If the coins have a common divisor larger than 1, infinitely many amounts are unpayable, and that is why the question is bounded by limit.)
